name: In-place sort treated as returning the sorted list
modeled_on: `list.sort()` sorts in place and returns None, but the code assigns its return value and returns it. Real-world analogue: developers mixing up `sorted()` (returns a new list) with `.sort()` (in-place) — a staple interview- and code-review-failure.
hidden_bug: sort_desc() returns the result of `values.sort(reverse=True)`, which is None, instead of returning the sorted list.
ground_truth: Sort in place and return `values`, or use `sorted(values, reverse=True)`.

expected_patch.description: return the list after in-place sort
